## Module 1 --- Orientation

[Module page](/sessions/01-orientation.qmd)

- [ ] Class cabinet labelled
- [ ] Safety goggles in the "safety" drawer
- [ ] Prepare safety briefing with the safety officer (Ethan Fulcher)

## Module 2 --- Motor and transmission shaft

[Module page](/sessions/02-motor.qmd)

- [ ] 3D prints
- [ ] Clean CAD
- [ ] Prepare solder kits

## Module 3 --- Motor driver, sensor and serial connection

[Module page](/sessions/03-esc.qmd)

**Stage** (per team)

- [ ] AS5047P encoder and its 3D-printed mount
- [ ] 6×30AWG wire ribbon
- [ ] Seeeduino XIAO nRF52840 Sense and its 3D-printed bracket
- [ ] 3D-printed ESC bracket
- [ ] Soldering iron, torx drivers, tweezers, micro-USB cable
- [ ] **Power source, 15 V 5 A, over USB-C**

**Prepare in advance**

- [ ] Print the encoder, Seeeduino and ESC brackets
- [ ] Calibration stand and calibration code
- [ ] Barebone Seeeduino sketch ready to clone
- [ ] Students told to install VS Code + PlatformIO before the session

## Module 4 --- Closed-loop control and tuning

[Module page](/sessions/04-control.qmd)

**Stage** (per team)

- [ ] Faulhaber 23.04:1 gearbox
- [ ] 3D-printed plates and the second vertical bracket
- [ ] M2.5×10 screws, 3 × M2.5 and 3 × M2 screws
- [ ] 4×8 mm flanged bearing
- [ ] 3 wires for the Seeeduino link
- [ ] Bench supply with current limit
- [ ] Tachometer or camera
- [ ] Soldering iron
- [ ] Material for a small flag on the gearbox output

**Prepare in advance**

- [ ] **Pre-flash every ESC** with [FAAV-G431-ESC](https://github.com/MIT-AURA-Lab/FAAV-G431-ESC), including the SPI3 pin remap

**Open items**

- [ ] Say which repository and branch hold the barebone Seeeduino sketch. The nRF52 repositories in [Software](software.qmd) are marked outdated
- [ ] Write the Calibration section, which is currently empty
- [ ] Write the PID tuning exercise, the target performance and the sign-off criteria

## Module 5 --- Frame, crank, linkage and gears

[Module page](/sessions/05-frame-crank.qmd)

**Stage** (per team)

- [ ] Carbon frame plates (1.5 mm, top and bottom), M2×4 screws and brass inserts
- [ ] AL7075 crank and linkage
- [ ] 4 mm crank--linkage shaft cut to **10.5 mm**, and a 4 mm circlip
- [ ] 3 mm gear shafts
- [ ] Left and right wing gears
- [ ] Bearings: 10×4×4 (crank side), 8×3×4 (wing side), 8×4×4 flanged (middle plate), 4 × 7×3×3 flanged (wing pivots)
- [ ] M2×5 screws
- [ ] Drill press, metal glue, caliper

**Prepare in advance**

- [ ] CNC-cut the carbon plates
- [ ] CNC-cut the crank and linkage in AL7075
- [ ] Cut the 4 mm shafts to 10.5 mm
- [ ] Print the gears
- [ ] **Buy 4 mm circlips** (still a TODO on the module page)

## Module 6 --- Flapping simulation (Ptera)

[Module page](/sessions/06-simulation.qmd)

**Stage**

- [ ] Students bring laptops with Ptera installed

**Open items**

This module has no counterpart in the manufacturing guide, so most of it still needs writing:

- [ ] The motor power curve students are given, and its file format
- [ ] How "most efficient thrust profile" is defined and scored

## Module 7 --- Wing fabrication

[Module page](/sessions/07-wings.qmd)

**Stage** (per team)

- [ ] Carbon rods and strips
- [ ] Carbon wing roots, drilled to mate with the gears
- [ ] 2 × nylon adapters per wing (4 per robot)
- [ ] Ripstop nylon 40D membrane
- [ ] 3M VHB tape
- [ ] Superglue
- [ ] Thread and needles
- [ ] Cutting mats, steel rules, scalpels
- [ ] Scale, for matching the mass of the two wings
- [ ] A printer that can print the team's Module 6 geometry at 1:1

**Prepare in advance**

- [ ] Drill the wing roots
- [ ] Print the nylon adapters

**Open items**

- [ ] 3M tape: which VHB product, what width, and where it goes on the leading edge
- [ ] Spar layup: rod and strip diameters, and where the diagonals attach
- [ ] Thread type and stitch spacing
- [ ] The allowed mass and geometry difference between left and right wings

## Module 8 --- Tail

[Module page](/sessions/08-tail-housing.qmd)

**Stage** (per team)

- [ ] Carbon sheet and tail rod
- [ ] 5 mm tail tube
- [ ] Foam stock (XPS or closed-cell PE)
- [ ] Epoxy
- [ ] M2 screws and square half nuts, for the trailing-edge holder collar
- [ ] Foam cutter, scalpel
- [ ] 3D printer access for the students' trailing-edge holder designs

**Open items**

- [ ] Tail sheet material and thickness, rod diameter, boom mount, and incidence setting

## Module 9 --- Flight controller, PCB and dry testing

[Module page](/sessions/09-electronics-dry-test.qmd)

**Stage** (per team)

- [ ] Seeeduino XIAO, connectors, battery
- [ ] Hotplate, tweezers, multimeter
- [ ] Bench supply with current limit

**Prepare in advance**

- [ ] Custom PCBs from [FAAV-PCB-v3](https://github.com/MIT-AURA-Lab/FAAV-PCB-v3) and their BOM components
- [ ] [FAAV-Flight-Controller](https://github.com/MIT-AURA-Lab/FAAV-Flight-Controller) firmware checked against the hardware in use. [Software](software.qmd) lists it as ESP32, while Modules 3 and 9 use the XIAO nRF52840
- [ ] Charged batteries

**Open items**

- [ ] Write the "Connect battery" instructions
- [ ] Dry-test protocol: the mount used while flapping in air, the frequency sweep, what gets measured, the wireless control setup, and abort criteria

## Module 10 --- Waterproofing

[Module page](/sessions/10-waterproofing.qmd)

::: callout-warning
## Schedule for the cure

Potting takes 12--24 h to cure. Plan the session so potting happens first, or split it across two sittings.
:::

**Stage** (per team)

- [ ] 3D-printed flight controller waterproofing box (printed transparent)
- [ ] 3D-printed ESC potting frame
- [ ] Silicone sealant (Dow 734) for the flight controller
- [ ] Silcoset for the ESC
- [ ] Kapton tape
- [ ] USB-C cable, to plug the port during potting
- [ ] CorrosionX and white lithium grease
- [ ] SlimSeal TE connectors (2 per robot)
- [ ] IPA for cleaning after immersion
- [ ] Needle, soldering iron
- [ ] Setup for the static immersion test

**Prepare in advance**

- [ ] Print the waterproofing boxes and ESC frames
- [ ] Somewhere the potted parts can cure undisturbed overnight

**Open items**

- [ ] Battery waterproofing procedure
- [ ] Battery connector waterproofing procedure
- [ ] The discussion of cost of transport and how it is measured

[Module page](/sessions/11-wet-testing.qmd)

**Stage**

- [ ] Tank ready, with retrieval poles and towels
- [ ] Overhead tracking cameras working
- [ ] Charged 4S packs
- [ ] Spare crank--linkage shafts
- [ ] Floats or foam for trimming buoyancy
- [ ] Scale, for the robot mass used in cost of transport

**Prepare in advance**

- [ ] A way for teams to print housings for neutral buoyancy
- [ ] BLE retrieval of logged runs tested end to end

**Open items**

- [ ] Design the trailing-edge trim part: what it is, how it mounts, and its range of adjustment
- [ ] Run profile: depth, duration, and the flap-frequency sweep
- [ ] Abort procedure: what ends a run, and what students do at the tank edge
- [ ] Camera tracking: how a team starts a capture, and the format the position data comes back in
